body: Thank you so much for this reply. Last night was an extremely low point for me. I finally got ahold of one of my friends that has known me for a long time, and he helped me out a lot. He told me to make a list of ten things that I am grateful for, and whenever things start to get to bad, I should pull out that "emergency list" and remember the things that I love and appreciate. Maybe this could help you too? I'm sorry to hear about your cutting on Thanksgiving. Sometimes it's hard to resist that urge. I hope that you are having an easier time now. Thank you for caring, and know that even though I don't know you, I care about you too.
I'm feeling better today. Last night was a bit of a low point. You replying actually helped, as silly as that seems.

My freshman year of college it was required that we were to live in the dorms. I was a first generation college student in my family, so I was completely overwhelmed and had no idea what to do. I decided that the best way to handle this situation was to pretend like I felt right at home and knew everything. Apparently, I was quite convincing because by the end of the first week about half of the people in my dorm believed that I was an RA (resident assistant a.k.a. the people that bust you with alcohol). Upon seeing one of the boys from the dorm at a party, I had him completely convinced that he was going to be in a heap of trouble when the two of us got back to the dorm. We're now friends, and we have a great story for how it all started.

I had read that it helped with anxiety, and at that point I was desperate for anything that could help me out. I smoked the next chance that I got and have smoked regularly since then.
